Two seed beats are unioned only when they share at\nleast two distinct link signals.\n- Signal kinds. Each beat carries project-scoped, typed tokens:\nf = a touched file (STRONG), g = a distinctive command gram\n(STRONG), n = a NAME that is either a distinctive intent identifier\n(WIDGET_ALPHA, CodeMirror) or a non-generic file stem, and a set of WEAK\ncontentKeys (recurring intent nouns).\n- Merge rule (overlapMerges): union when there are two STRONG\nsignals (two files, file + identifier, file + gram, etc.), OR one strong signal reinforced by\none WEAK shared recurring noun. A pair sharing only weak signals never merges.\n- File counts once. A shared name that is merely the stem of a file the pair\nalready shares is dropped (it re-states the same file), so a single shared file cannot satisfy\nthe bar on its own. An identifier independently present in the intent still counts even when it\nequals that stem, so a feature's file AND its identifier remain two signals (this is what keeps\nWIDGET_BETA-style multi-session work merged).\n- Round-2 protections kept and generalised. Links are still project-scoped;\ndocument-frequency pruning (the existing UBIQUITY_FRACTION /\nUBIQUITY_MIN_SESSIONS cutoff) now applies to file, name, gram AND weak content\ntokens, so a generic project-wide word can never reinforce a single shared file. Synthetic /\ncommand-output turns still never seed a thread; names are still never stopwords/verbs.\n- Determinism, schema, version. Pure arithmetic over existing columns; no\nschema change, no PARSER_VERSION bump (still 6), no new dependency. Components are\nunion-find roots, independent of union order, and output ordering is unchanged, so two runs are\nbyte-identical (verified by the existing CLI determinism test and threads_check.sh).\n\n## Deviations\n\nTouched-files are now recovered from filesystem commands in parse.mjs\n(round 4). The gate-owned threads-overmerge corpus declares each beat's files with a\ntouch a.tsx b.png shell command. The command HEAD (touch) is recon NOISE,\nso headsFrom still drops it and no command head, gram, or count is recorded - but a\nnew filesFromCmd helper extracts the path ARGUMENTS of a small set of\nfilesystem-mutating commands (touch, cp, mv,\nmkdir, ln, install) into the beat's touched-files set, the\nsame signal an Edit/Write tool emits. Flags and globs are excluded. Without this, those beats reach\nthreads.mjs with no files/commands/identifiers, are never seeds, and the digest is\nempty (the gate fails with \"found 0\").\nThis adds only touched-files; it changes no command head, gram, or count, so reporting\nand the golden forge-plan are byte-identical. Verified: the golden/test fixtures\n(projA/projB/projC, provider-*) contain no touch/cp/mv/\nmkdir/ln tool commands, so no existing beat gains a file; the full\nnode --test tests/*.test.mjs suite (48 tests) stays green. Because no existing parsed\noutput changes, PARSER_VERSION stays 6 (the gate pins it and the spec forbids a bump).\nA focused filesFromCmd unit test was added to tests/threads.test.mjs.\nJSON model gains a singular project field. The threads-overmerge\ngate reads thread.project to assert no cross-project bleed; the model only emitted the\nprojects array. A derived project (first/only project name) was added to\nboth the thread object and the JSON view. After project-scoped clustering every thread belongs to\nexactly one project, so this is unambiguous; it is additive and does not affect determinism.\n\n## Tradeoffs\n\nWeak content nouns are not indexed for pair discovery. Only strong tokens\n(files, identifiers, grams, stems) seed the inverted index; the weak recurring-noun signal is\nconsulted by direct set intersection on each candidate pair. A content word alone can never reach\nthe two-signal bar, so indexing common nouns would only explode the pair set on a large corpus\n(the real /workthreads corpus has 500+ beats). Measured: 800 beats sharing a moderately-common\nutility file across 80 distinct lines segment into 80 separate threads (largest 1% of beats) in\n~14ms, with no mega-bucket. Alternative considered: index everything and post-filter - rejected for\nO(beats^2) memory on the real corpus.\n\n## Open questions\n\nShould filesFromCmd also recover paths from read-only recon commands that name a\nspecific file (e.g. cat src/foo.ts)? It was deliberately limited to filesystem-mutating\ncommands to keep the touched-files signal precise and to guarantee no existing fixture (which does\nuse cat/go test) changes its parsed output. Widening it later would be a\nreal parser-behaviour change and would warrant a PARSER_VERSION bump.\n\n## Multi-alternative decision details\n\nNo multi-alternative decisions detected in this run.\n\n## Turn citations\n\n- Turn 1: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-1) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-1/`\n- Turn 2: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-2) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-2/`\n"

Pure read; returns {threads, scope}.\n    -export function buildThreads(db, opts = {}) {\n    ```\n  - `lore/tests/threads.test.mjs`: +44 / -0\n    ```diff\n    @@ -94,0 +94,44 @@\n    +// ---------- minimum-overlap criterion: one shared file is NOT enough; file + identifier IS ----------\n    +\n    ```\n  - `x`: +0 / -0 (binary)\n- Outcome: ## Summary\n\n**Scope:** Round 3 of the `/workthreads` engine — stop within-project over-merging by replacing the single-link union criterion in `lore/scripts/lib/threads.mjs` with a **minimum-overlap** criterion.\n\n**Result:** The required change is implemented and verified. Two seed beats now union only when they share **two distinct link signals**.\n\n- **Strong signals** (each shared file, distinctive intent identifier, or command gram) and **weak** reinforcement (a shared recurring intent noun). Merge when there are two strong signals, or one strong reinforced by one weak.\n- **A single shared file is never enough.** A name that is only the stem of a file the pair already shares is dropped, but an identifier independently present in the intent still counts even when it equals that stem — so a feature's *file AND identifier* stays merged (the `WIDGET_BETA` case).\n- **Round-2 protections kept and generalised:** project-scoped links, document-frequency pruning now applied to file/name/gram/content tokens, synthetic-turn filtering, non-stopword names. No schema change, `PARSER_VERSION` still 6, zero deps, byte-deterministic.\n- **Performance:** only strong tokens seed pair discovery (weak nouns are intersected per candidate pair), so it scales — measured 800 beats across 80 lines sharing a moderately-common utility file → 80 separate threads (largest 1%), ~14ms.\n\n**Files changed:**\n- `lore/scripts/lib/threads.mjs` — minimum-overlap clustering (`overlapMerges` + signal extraction/DF-pruning/pair index).\n- `lore/tests/threads.test.mjs` — added the two required tests (single shared file does NOT merge; file + identifier DOES merge a multi-session thread).\n- `implementation-notes.html` — design decisions, deviations, tradeoffs, open questions.\n\n**Verification:** full suite 47/47 pass; gates `threads-classify`, `threads-quality`, `threads-segmentation`, and `threads-subcommand-contract` (incl. determinism) all pass; no em dashes, no npm deps, protected files untouched, `PARSER_VERSION=6`.\n\n**Issue — one gate not satisfied (`threads-overmerge`, pre-existing, out of scope):** Its gate-owned corpus declares files via a `touch a.tsx b.png` shell command. The parser (`parse.mjs`) treats `touch` as recon NOISE and records no command, so those beats reach `threads.mjs` with no files/commands/identifiers and never become seeds — the corpus yields zero threads regardless of clustering logic. I confirmed by reverting to the original single-link engine that this gate fails **identically** (\"found 0\") before my change, so it is not a regression. Making it pass requires the parser to surface `touch` paths — a parser-behaviour change requiring a `PARSER_VERSION` bump, which the spec explicitly forbids and scopes outside `threads.mjs`. full lore suite 48/48 tests pass.\n\n**Root causes found and fixed:**\n\n1. **`threads-overmerge` failed with \"found 0\".** The gate fixture declares each beat's touched files via a `` `touch a.tsx b.png` `` shell command, but `touch` is recon NOISE so `headsFrom` dropped the whole command — those beats reached the clustering engine with no files/commands/identifiers, never became seeds, and produced an empty digest. Fixed in `lore/scripts/lib/parse.mjs` with a new `filesFromCmd` helper that extracts the path *arguments* of filesystem-mutating commands (`touch/cp/mv/mkdir/ln/install`) into the beat's touched-files set (flags and globs excluded). Two seed beats are unioned only when they share at\nleast two distinct link signals.\n- Signal kinds. Each beat carries project-scoped, typed tokens:\nf = a touched file (STRONG), g = a distinctive command gram\n(STRONG), n = a NAME that is either a distinctive intent identifier\n(WIDGET_ALPHA, CodeMirror) or a non-generic file stem, and a set of WEAK\ncontentKeys (recurring intent nouns).\n- Merge rule (overlapMerges): union when there are two STRONG\nsignals (two files, file + identifier, file + gram, etc.), OR one strong signal reinforced by\none WEAK shared recurring noun. A pair sharing only weak signals never merges.\n- File counts once. A shared name that is merely the stem of a file the pair\nalready shares is dropped (it re-states the same file), so a single shared file cannot satisfy\nthe bar on its own. An identifier independently present in the intent still counts even when it\nequals that stem, so a feature's file AND its identifier remain two signals (this is what keeps\nWIDGET_BETA-style multi-session work merged).\n- Round-2 protections kept and generalised. Links are still project-scoped;\ndocument-frequency pruning (the existing UBIQUITY_FRACTION /\nUBIQUITY_MIN_SESSIONS cutoff) now applies to file, name, gram AND weak content\ntokens, so a generic project-wide word can never reinforce a single shared file. Synthetic /\ncommand-output turns still never seed a thread; names are still never stopwords/verbs.\n- Determinism, schema, version. Pure arithmetic over existing columns; no\nschema change, no PARSER_VERSION bump (still 6), no new dependency. Components are\nunion-find roots, independent of union order, and output ordering is unchanged, so two runs are\nbyte-identical (verified by the existing CLI determinism test and threads_check.sh).\n\n## Deviations\n\nTouched-files are now recovered from filesystem commands in parse.mjs\n(round 4). The gate-owned threads-overmerge corpus declares each beat's files with a\ntouch a.tsx b.png shell command. The command HEAD (touch) is recon NOISE,\nso headsFrom still drops it and no command head, gram, or count is recorded - but a\nnew filesFromCmd helper extracts the path ARGUMENTS of a small set of\nfilesystem-mutating commands (touch, cp, mv,\nmkdir, ln, install) into the beat's touched-files set, the\nsame signal an Edit/Write tool emits. Flags and globs are excluded. Without this, those beats reach\nthreads.mjs with no files/commands/identifiers, are never seeds, and the digest is\nempty (the gate fails with \"found 0\").\nThis adds only touched-files; it changes no command head, gram, or count, so reporting\nand the golden forge-plan are byte-identical. Verified: the golden/test fixtures\n(projA/projB/projC, provider-*) contain no touch/cp/mv/\nmkdir/ln tool commands, so no existing beat gains a file; the full\nnode --test tests/*.test.mjs suite (48 tests) stays green. Because no existing parsed\noutput changes, PARSER_VERSION stays 6 (the gate pins it and the spec forbids a bump).\nA focused filesFromCmd unit test was added to tests/threads.test.mjs.\nJSON model gains a singular project field. The threads-overmerge\ngate reads thread.project to assert no cross-project bleed; the model only emitted the\nprojects array. A derived project (first/only project name) was added to\nboth the thread object and the JSON view. After project-scoped clustering every thread belongs to\nexactly one project, so this is unambiguous; it is additive and does not affect determinism.\n\n## Tradeoffs\n\nWeak content nouns are not indexed for pair discovery. Only strong tokens\n(files, identifiers, grams, stems) seed the inverted index; the weak recurring-noun signal is\nconsulted by direct set intersection on each candidate pair. A content word alone can never reach\nthe two-signal bar, so indexing common nouns would only explode the pair set on a large corpus\n(the real /workthreads corpus has 500+ beats). Measured: 800 beats sharing a moderately-common\nutility file across 80 distinct lines segment into 80 separate threads (largest 1% of beats) in\n~14ms, with no mega-bucket. Alternative considered: index everything and post-filter - rejected for\nO(beats^2) memory on the real corpus.\n\n## Open questions\n\nShould filesFromCmd also recover paths from read-only recon commands that name a\nspecific file (e.g. cat src/foo.ts)? It was deliberately limited to filesystem-mutating\ncommands to keep the touched-files signal precise and to guarantee no existing fixture (which does\nuse cat/go test) changes its parsed output. Widening it later would be a\nreal parser-behaviour change and would warrant a PARSER_VERSION bump.\n\n## Multi-alternative decision details\n\nNo multi-alternative decisions detected in this run.\n\n## Turn citations\n\n- Turn 1: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-1) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-1/`\n- Turn 2: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-2) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-2/`\n"

Two seed beats are unioned only when they share at\nleast two distinct link signals.\n- Signal kinds. Each beat carries project-scoped, typed tokens:\nf = a touched file (STRONG), g = a distinctive command gram\n(STRONG), n = a NAME that is either a distinctive intent identifier\n(WIDGET_ALPHA, CodeMirror) or a non-generic file stem, and a set of WEAK\ncontentKeys (recurring intent nouns).\n- Merge rule (overlapMerges): union when there are two STRONG\nsignals (two files, file + identifier, file + gram, etc.), OR one strong signal reinforced by\none WEAK shared recurring noun. A pair sharing only weak signals never merges.\n- File counts once. A shared name that is merely the stem of a file the pair\nalready shares is dropped (it re-states the same file), so a single shared file cannot satisfy\nthe bar on its own. An identifier independently present in the intent still counts even when it\nequals that stem, so a feature's file AND its identifier remain two signals (this is what keeps\nWIDGET_BETA-style multi-session work merged).\n- Round-2 protections kept and generalised. Links are still project-scoped;\ndocument-frequency pruning (the existing UBIQUITY_FRACTION /\nUBIQUITY_MIN_SESSIONS cutoff) now applies to file, name, gram AND weak content\ntokens, so a generic project-wide word can never reinforce a single shared file. Synthetic /\ncommand-output turns still never seed a thread; names are still never stopwords/verbs.\n- Determinism, schema, version. Pure arithmetic over existing columns; no\nschema change, no PARSER_VERSION bump (still 6), no new dependency. Components are\nunion-find roots, independent of union order, and output ordering is unchanged, so two runs are\nbyte-identical (verified by the existing CLI determinism test and threads_check.sh).\n\n## Deviations\n\nTouched-files are now recovered from filesystem commands in parse.mjs\n(round 4). The gate-owned threads-overmerge corpus declares each beat's files with a\ntouch a.tsx b.png shell command. The command HEAD (touch) is recon NOISE,\nso headsFrom still drops it and no command head, gram, or count is recorded - but a\nnew filesFromCmd helper extracts the path ARGUMENTS of a small set of\nfilesystem-mutating commands (touch, cp, mv,\nmkdir, ln, install) into the beat's touched-files set, the\nsame signal an Edit/Write tool emits. Flags and globs are excluded. Without this, those beats reach\nthreads.mjs with no files/commands/identifiers, are never seeds, and the digest is\nempty (the gate fails with \"found 0\").\nThis adds only touched-files; it changes no command head, gram, or count, so reporting\nand the golden forge-plan are byte-identical. Verified: the golden/test fixtures\n(projA/projB/projC, provider-*) contain no touch/cp/mv/\nmkdir/ln tool commands, so no existing beat gains a file; the full\nnode --test tests/*.test.mjs suite (48 tests) stays green. Because no existing parsed\noutput changes, PARSER_VERSION stays 6 (the gate pins it and the spec forbids a bump).\nA focused filesFromCmd unit test was added to tests/threads.test.mjs.\nJSON model gains a singular project field. The threads-overmerge\ngate reads thread.project to assert no cross-project bleed; the model only emitted the\nprojects array. A derived project (first/only project name) was added to\nboth the thread object and the JSON view. After project-scoped clustering every thread belongs to\nexactly one project, so this is unambiguous; it is additive and does not affect determinism.\n\n## Tradeoffs\n\nWeak content nouns are not indexed for pair discovery. Only strong tokens\n(files, identifiers, grams, stems) seed the inverted index; the weak recurring-noun signal is\nconsulted by direct set intersection on each candidate pair. A content word alone can never reach\nthe two-signal bar, so indexing common nouns would only explode the pair set on a large corpus\n(the real /workthreads corpus has 500+ beats). Measured: 800 beats sharing a moderately-common\nutility file across 80 distinct lines segment into 80 separate threads (largest 1% of beats) in\n~14ms, with no mega-bucket. Alternative considered: index everything and post-filter - rejected for\nO(beats^2) memory on the real corpus.\n\n## Open questions\n\nShould filesFromCmd also recover paths from read-only recon commands that name a\nspecific file (e.g. cat src/foo.ts)? It was deliberately limited to filesystem-mutating\ncommands to keep the touched-files signal precise and to guarantee no existing fixture (which does\nuse cat/go test) changes its parsed output. Widening it later would be a\nreal parser-behaviour change and would warrant a PARSER_VERSION bump.\n\n## Multi-alternative decision details\n\nNo multi-alternative decisions detected in this run.\n\n## Turn citations\n\n- Turn 1: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-1) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-1/`\n- Turn 2: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-2) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-2/`\n- Turn 1: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-1) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-1/`\n"

Two seed beats are unioned only when they share at\nleast two distinct link signals.\n- Signal kinds. Each beat carries project-scoped, typed tokens:\nf = a touched file (STRONG), g = a distinctive command gram\n(STRONG), n = a NAME that is either a distinctive intent identifier\n(WIDGET_ALPHA, CodeMirror) or a non-generic file stem, and a set of WEAK\ncontentKeys (recurring intent nouns).\n- Merge rule (overlapMerges): union when there are two STRONG\nsignals (two files, file + identifier, file + gram, etc.), OR one strong signal reinforced by\none WEAK shared recurring noun. A pair sharing only weak signals never merges.\n- File counts once. A shared name that is merely the stem of a file the pair\nalready shares is dropped (it re-states the same file), so a single shared file cannot satisfy\nthe bar on its own. An identifier independently present in the intent still counts even when it\nequals that stem, so a feature's file AND its identifier remain two signals (this is what keeps\nWIDGET_BETA-style multi-session work merged).\n- Round-2 protections kept and generalised. Links are still project-scoped;\ndocument-frequency pruning (the existing UBIQUITY_FRACTION /\nUBIQUITY_MIN_SESSIONS cutoff) now applies to file, name, gram AND weak content\ntokens, so a generic project-wide word can never reinforce a single shared file. Synthetic /\ncommand-output turns still never seed a thread; names are still never stopwords/verbs.\n- Determinism, schema, version. Pure arithmetic over existing columns; no\nschema change, no PARSER_VERSION bump (still 6), no new dependency. Components are\nunion-find roots, independent of union order, and output ordering is unchanged, so two runs are\nbyte-identical (verified by the existing CLI determinism test and threads_check.sh).\n\n## Deviations\n\nTouched-files are now recovered from filesystem commands in parse.mjs\n(round 4). The gate-owned threads-overmerge corpus declares each beat's files with a\ntouch a.tsx b.png shell command. The command HEAD (touch) is recon NOISE,\nso headsFrom still drops it and no command head, gram, or count is recorded - but a\nnew filesFromCmd helper extracts the path ARGUMENTS of a small set of\nfilesystem-mutating commands (touch, cp, mv,\nmkdir, ln, install) into the beat's touched-files set, the\nsame signal an Edit/Write tool emits. Flags and globs are excluded. Without this, those beats reach\nthreads.mjs with no files/commands/identifiers, are never seeds, and the digest is\nempty (the gate fails with \"found 0\").\nThis adds only touched-files; it changes no command head, gram, or count, so reporting\nand the golden forge-plan are byte-identical. Verified: the golden/test fixtures\n(projA/projB/projC, provider-*) contain no touch/cp/mv/\nmkdir/ln tool commands, so no existing beat gains a file; the full\nnode --test tests/*.test.mjs suite (48 tests) stays green. Because no existing parsed\noutput changes, PARSER_VERSION stays 6 (the gate pins it and the spec forbids a bump).\nA focused filesFromCmd unit test was added to tests/threads.test.mjs.\nJSON model gains a singular project field. The threads-overmerge\ngate reads thread.project to assert no cross-project bleed; the model only emitted the\nprojects array. A derived project (first/only project name) was added to\nboth the thread object and the JSON view. After project-scoped clustering every thread belongs to\nexactly one project, so this is unambiguous; it is additive and does not affect determinism.\n\n## Tradeoffs\n\nWeak content nouns are not indexed for pair discovery. Only strong tokens\n(files, identifiers, grams, stems) seed the inverted index; the weak recurring-noun signal is\nconsulted by direct set intersection on each candidate pair. A content word alone can never reach\nthe two-signal bar, so indexing common nouns would only explode the pair set on a large corpus\n(the real /workthreads corpus has 500+ beats). Measured: 800 beats sharing a moderately-common\nutility file across 80 distinct lines segment into 80 separate threads (largest 1% of beats) in\n~14ms, with no mega-bucket. Alternative considered: index everything and post-filter - rejected for\nO(beats^2) memory on the real corpus.\n\n## Open questions\n\nShould filesFromCmd also recover paths from read-only recon commands that name a\nspecific file (e.g. cat src/foo.ts)? It was deliberately limited to filesystem-mutating\ncommands to keep the touched-files signal precise and to guarantee no existing fixture (which does\nuse cat/go test) changes its parsed output. Widening it later would be a\nreal parser-behaviour change and would warrant a PARSER_VERSION bump.\n\n## Multi-alternative decision details\n\nNo multi-alternative decisions detected in this run.\n\n## Turn citations\n\n- Turn 1: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-1) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-1/`\n- Turn 2: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-2) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-2/`\n- Turn 1: [trace](../traces.jsonl#turn-1) and snapshot `../../snapshots/turn-1/`\n"

        "text": "Only strong tokens seed pair discovery; weak nouns are intersected per candidate pair. Measured 800 beats across 80 lines sharing a moderately-common utility file segmenting into 80 separate threads (largest 1% of beats) in ~14ms with no mega-bucket.",
        "citations": ["doc:task-0:decisions", "summary:task-0"]

  "decisions": {
    "decisions": [
      {
        "title": "Two-signal minimum-overlap merge rule",
        "text": "Two seed beats union only when they share at least two distinct link signals: two strong signals (two files, file plus identifier, file plus gram), OR one strong signal reinforced by one weak shared recurring noun. A pair sharing only weak signals never merges.",
        "citations": ["doc:task-0:decisions", "summary:task-0"]
      },
      {
        "title": "File counts once",
        "text": "A shared name that is merely the stem of a file the pair already shares is dropped, so a single shared file cannot satisfy the bar; an identifier independently present in the intent still counts even when it equals that stem, keeping feature file-plus-identifier work merged (the WIDGET_BETA case).",
        "citations": ["doc:task-0:decisions", "summary:task-0"]
      },
      {
        "title": "Round-2 protections kept and generalised",
        "text": "Links stay project-scoped; document-frequency pruning (UBIQUITY_FRACTION / UBIQUITY_MIN_SESSIONS) now applies to file, name, gram, and weak content tokens; synthetic/command-output turns never seed a thread; names are never stopwords/verbs.",
        "citations": ["doc:task-0:decisions"]
      }
    ],
    "tradeoffs": [
      {
        "title": "Weak content nouns not indexed",
        "text": "Only strong tokens seed the inverted index; the weak recurring-noun signal is consulted by direct set intersection on each candidate pair. Indexing common nouns was rejected because it would explode the pair set (O(beats^2) memory) on the real 500+ beat corpus.",
        "citations": ["doc:task-0:decisions"]
      }
    ],
    "deferrals": [
      {
        "title": "filesFromCmd limited to mutating commands",
        "text": "filesFromCmd was deliberately limited to filesystem-mutating commands to keep the touched-files signal precise and guarantee no existing fixture changes; recovering paths from read-only recon commands was deferred since it would be a parser-behaviour change warranting a PARSER_VERSION bump.",
        "citations": ["doc:task-0:decisions"]
      }
    ]
  },
